cards.text: Peter just asked Jesus what the disciples will get for leaving everything to follow Him, and Jesus promised them a reward. Now Jesus tells them a story: the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who goes out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard. EARLY, friend, before the snooze button even gets its first hit.

cards.question: Before the landowner sends the early workers into his vineyard, he makes a deal with them. He agrees to pay them a ___ for the day.

cards.text: About the third hour, the landowner heads back out and sees more people standing in the marketplace doing nothing. And friend, I KNOW that look from my years in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The landowner tells the people from the marketplace to go into his vineyard too. What does he promise them?

answers.text: I will pay you whatever is right
I will pay you half the day's wage
I will pay you once the harvest is in

cards.question: So the third-hour workers head into the vineyard. True or false: about the sixth hour and again about the ninth hour, the landowner goes out and does the same thing.

cards.text: About the eleventh hour, he finds still others standing around and asks why they've been standing there all day long doing nothing. The ELEVENTH hour, friend, that's walking into the party while they're stacking up the chairs.

cards.question: The eleventh-hour workers tell the landowner they've been standing around because no one has ___ them.
With the day almost over, the landowner sends the eleventh-hour workers into his vineyard too.

cards.text: When evening comes, the owner tells his foreman to call the workers in and pay them their wages. PAYDAY, the best word in the world after preheat.

cards.question: In what order does the landowner tell his foreman to pay the workers?
The workers hired about the eleventh hour put in about one hour. How much does each of them receive?

cards.text: Now the early morning crew steps up, and they assume they'll receive more. I can see them counting on their fingers like they just WON something.

cards.question: The workers hired early in the morning each receive more than a denarius.
On receiving their pay, the early workers begin to ___ against the ___.

cards.text: The early crew says the last ones worked only one hour, but he made them equal to the crew who bore the burden and the scorching heat of the day. The scorching heat, friend, they want EVERYBODY to know they sweated.

cards.question: The landowner calls one of the grumblers Friend and says he's not being unfair to him. What does he remind him of?

answers.text: He owes me for his tools
He was warned about the heat

cards.text: The landowner tells the grumbler to take his pay and go. He wants to give the last man hired the SAME as this sunrise worker got, and friend, I bet that jaw hits the dirt.

cards.question: The landowner asks if he has the right to do as he pleases with what is his. Then he asks the grumbler one more question. What is it?

answers.text: Are you envious because I am generous
Are you tired because the day was long
Are you angry because the work was hard

cards.text: Jesus wraps it up: “So the last will be first, and the first will be last.” Friend, I spent years at the very back of a junk drawer, so that line hits me RIGHT in the apron.

findings.problem: The answers don't match each other. 'He agreed to one denarius' and 'He was warned about the heat' talk about the grumbler in the third person. 'He owes me for his tools' switches to the landowner speaking as 'me', so it reads as a different kind of answer and makes the right one easier to spot.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card calls the grumbler 'this sunrise worker'. The text only says the landowner went out 'early in the morning' (Matthew 20:1). It never says sunrise, so the card adds a time the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
